correctness.rationale: For odd n>=3 every edge lies on one unique row/column/sum line, and every noncollinear clique is a mixed triangle; an exceptional four-clique would require 2d=0, ruled out by odd n. All higher line simplices collapse, while row-column rectangles fill using mixed triangles, proving simple connectivity and reduced homology concentrated in degree two. The Euler characteristic 1+(n-1)^3 fixes the integral H2 rank. Translations outside three direction subgroups stabilize no simplex; a nonzero translation within one stabilizes exactly n line simplices, each with contractible geometric fixed set. The Lefschetz traces are therefore identity (n-1)^3, n-1 for a direction translation, -1 otherwise. Orthogonality of Z_n^2 characters produces exactly m_{r,s}=n-3+1_{r=0}+1_{s=0}+1_{r=s}-1_{(r,s)=0}. New independent full-clique, simplex and signed-Lefschetz enumerations for n=3,5,7 verify all translates, including small cases, but the odd-order argument is the unrestricted proof.

The parameter family and group action are canonical rather than arbitrary.
